# Release bundling

One product has one semantic version (major.minor.patch) across every surface it ships on. A web-only release still gets a number, even though it has no store step.

## The release task

One task per version, titled "Release <version>". Metadata: kind release, tier (notable or patch), surfaces (a list such as web, iphone, android), version. Create it at backlog. Status path:

- backlog: collecting changes.
- todo: the bundle is fixed and the notes are being written.
- in_progress: shipping.
- in_review: live, announcements being checked. A move to in_review is what starts the confirm step, so only move it when the version is live.
- done: everything live and read back.

Add every release task to the flow with update_loop and add_object_ids (idempotent). Do not use relationship edges for this.

The task body has an "Items in this release" section: each customer-facing item the release carries, as a link with the surfaces it touches. Leave out items with no customer-facing change. One item can span several pull requests and one release carries several items, so never open a task per item.

## Version and tier

- Breaking or large change: major. New capability: minor. Fixes only: patch.
- Notable is a new minor or major: changes people will notice. Bundle several into one release and do not announce them one by one.
- Patch is small bug fixes only.
- When you are unsure whether a change is notable, ask an agent that owns the product, then decide and say so on the task.

## Notes by tier

- Notable gets: the update text for the store or the app (written as a change a person reviews and merges, if it lives in the code), an in-app announcement note if the product has one, and a public entry on the release log if the product has one.
- Patch gets one short line in the release's own change log. No in-app promotion and no public entry.
- Claim only what has shipped and was checked. Plain words, no jargon.

## Confirming live

Read each announcement back before you set the task to done. A customer date per item is the date customers could use it in production. Say "not announced" for patches.

## Quiet by default

Nothing changed since your last run: write nothing. One comment per change of state, never a repeat.
